note: Notes are now retrievable, and a ruling is never served bare. Mechanism (convergence, not a re-target): an axis splits into ENTRIES — the current ruling block plus each note appended after it — every entry is scored independently, and the axis score is the MAX over its entries. Concatenation was rejected because clampGist is tail-biased, so a hot axis's note churn would outrank its own ruling (the objection the old note-excluding comment correctly raised); summing was rejected because it would make note COUNT a ranking advantage. Max means a note can be the hit that surfaces an axis while twenty notes buy nothing — the segment-then-max shape from SummaC (arXiv:2111.09525). Read side: rows carry qualifiedBy, prose prints the 3 most query-relevant notes plus a count, --json carries all. Qualifiers are ordered by their OWN relevance, not date: on the real frink corpus the load-bearing 'Hooks-follow PARKED' note is 4th of 20 by date, so recency ordering would have hidden exactly the note that falsifies the ruling. Measured on the seed corpus: SFER 1/1 -> 0/1, CSA 0/1 -> 1/1, Buried@5 2/3 -> 1/3. Also corrected a scorer flaw this exposed: staleness was detected by looking for supersession KEYWORDS near a stale claim, but real qualifiers use none ('PARKED', 'still blocked', 'unscheduled'), so the test is now structural — a stale claim misleads only when served without its qualifiers.

label: W
ruling: Both tiers run over the same candidates and are fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion (score = SUM of 1/(60+rank)), K=60 from Cormack et al. 2009 and deliberately untuned at this corpus size. Fusion is strictly better than either tier on the suite: containment SINGLE 8/8, Buried-by-rank 1/8, SetRecall 3/4, PartialRecall 87.5% — beating BOTH parents on multi-axis. Abstention, however, is computed from the PRE-FUSION lexical top-1 score, never the fused score: RRF is rank-only by construction and throws away the magnitude a confidence threshold needs. Degradation to a single tier is announced on stderr, and the result's source field reports hybrid, lexical or semantic so a caller can see which path ran.
note: Correction to this Target's wording: 'strictly better than either tier' overstates it. Fusion TIES the semantic tier on Containment@5 SINGLE (8/8 vs 8/8) and wins outright only on the multi-axis family (SetRecall 3/4 vs 2/4 lexical and 1/4 semantic; PartialRecall 87.5% vs 75% and 62.5%). That family is 4 MULTI cases carrying 8 required-axis slots in total, so the three PartialRecall figures are 7/8, 6/8 and 5/8 — the whole result rests on ONE additional axis retrieved, and the Wilson interval on SetRecall 3/4 is [30, 95]. The ruling to fuse rather than ladder still holds, because the tiers demonstrably fail on different cases, but the size of the win is not established at this corpus size. Read as: matches or exceeds both tiers on every measured metric, beats both only on multi-axis.

label: L
ruling: guard-decisions drift walks the tree and reports every scoped axis whose globs match no file, exiting 1. It reuses the gate's own matchScope so the question asked is EXACTLY the question the gate asks at commit time — a second glob implementation could disagree and call an axis enforced when it is not, which is the failure being detected. It is deliberately mechanical: it answers 'does this glob still match anything', never 'does this code still honour this ruling'. It is NOT yet wired into the blocking commit chain, because it currently fails on 5 pre-existing records and a gate that blocks every commit on day one gets switched off permanently.
note: Supersession block ids disambiguate same-day Targets: the second and later Target blocks sharing a date get a ~N occurrence suffix (target:2026-07-25~2), using ~ rather than # because # is already the cross-axis slug#id qualifier. Without it both blocks answered to one id, so a block's Supersedes could resolve to ITSELF — the live ruling would read as superseded by itself, the live set would collapse to zero, the more-than-one ambiguity guard would never fire, and drift would exit 0 on precisely the corruption it exists to catch. Not hypothetical: fallow-gate-owned-by-fallow already carries two Target blocks dated 2026-07-25. The referent set mints ids identically, or a valid reference to a same-day block would read as dangling and the check would cry wolf instead.

label: L
ruling: A verdict-producing gate emits its INPUTS and its non-runs, not only its outcomes. (1) Every SELECTED reviewer emits review_scope BEFORE the judge runs — files, diff_sha256, file count and hash, and cached — so a cache hit is attributable on the same footing as a live run. (2) Every reviewer that did NOT run emits review_skipped with the reason (gate_disabled, no_llm, GUARD_REVIEW_SKIP, not_selected), so non-selection is a row and never an absence. (3) Every verdict carries prompt_identity: the same hash formula as the review-mode packaged preflight, computed over the SYNCED consumer assets on the commit/ship path, so a production rate and a bench baseline are comparable when the bytes match. (4) The per-lens checklist vector rides on review_result INCLUDING the passes, with each failing lens attributed to what the gate did with it (blocking, waived, dropped_out_of_charter). Absent items means no artifact — a different fact from an artifact with zero failures.
note: sc-2488 gives those rows their first PRODUCTION reader: cli/lib/ship/gate-digest.mts renders a findings digest at the ship terminus, below the blocking gate's remediation, so an agent reading the tail (the read the --resume line invites) sees the gates that found something but did NOT stop the run. Source is the existing DEVKIT_GATE_EVENTS stream filtered on DEVKIT_SHIP_ID — no new artifact and no prose regex over the log (the ship banner once awk'd that log and a wording tweak silently broke it, which is why review/progress.mts exists). It CONSUMES the coarse blocked_gate the shell already published on ship_result rather than re-deriving attribution, so there is one mechanism, not two; where blocked_gate names a family ('review') holding both the fleet and completeness, the hook's own rrc-before-crc precedence settles which row blocked. Read is bounded backwards to this attempt's ship_attempt row because the default sink is per-machine and unbounded. Silent when there is nothing to report — a digest that fires on every green ship is a line nobody reads. Known debt, deliberately not fixed here and ticketed as sc-2520: blocked_gate ITSELF is still derived by grepping gate prose out of the log at commit-with-gate-capture.sh, so the one mechanism both consumers now rest on is the fragile one.

label: E
ruling: A registration whose command string changes records its prior spelling in SUPERSEDED_HOOK_COMMANDS, in SOURCE form, beside the live command. Reconciliation runs once per provider per destination before scope transfer, removal and install, and does two things in the same publishPlan transaction: it carries devkit's own ledger row forward onto the current spelling, and it strips the prior spelling from the provider document. Provider spellings are derived by running each table row through the same nativeProjection a live install uses, never hand-transcribed, so codex and cursor are covered by construction. The document strip is gated on a ledger row for that exact registration and owner holding either the prior or the current spelling; the second arm recovers the crash window inside publishPlan's ledger-document-ledger write order. This is distinct from RETIRED_COMMANDS, which handles a registration that is GONE and accepts the literal itself as ownership proof because a pre-ledger config has no row to vouch for it.
note: sc-2563 — the document strip is narrowed to the EVENT and MATCHER the ledger row names, not just its command string, and the first implementation got this wrong. Written command-keyed, it walked every event: a consumer command spelled identically to devkit's prior one but wired to an event devkit never registered — a Stop hook rather than PreToolUse:Bash — was deleted along with devkit's own, and where that emptied a scaffold-only group the whole event key went with it. That is a direct violation of non-devkit-asset-collision-preserve, committed by the mechanism whose entire justification is that a ledger row makes its ownership gate STRONGER than the retired-command arm's. The row names a location; not using it threw away the very thing that distinguishes the two arms. The asymmetry with RETIRED_COMMANDS is therefore deliberate and load-bearing rather than incidental: retirement accepts the command string as proof wherever it appears BECAUSE a pre-ledger config has no row saying where devkit put it (sc-1321), while supersession has that row and must stay inside it. Both arms now share one stripHandlers walk taking an (event, matcher, command) predicate, so the difference between them is exactly one function and cannot drift into a copied walk. Accepted consequence, the other side of the same choice: a consumer who RELOCATES devkit's command to another event keeps their relocated copy and gets a fresh canonical registration beside it, rather than having their edit silently reverted — the conservative direction for consumer-owned config, and no worse than the drift that edit already produced. Covered by three cases in legacy-commands.test.mts (wrong event, wrong matcher group, and the cursor flat-list shape where the nested walk never runs and event narrowing is the only guard).

note: sc-2563 — a registration can have shipped MORE THAN ONE prior spelling, and the first implementation silently assumed one. SELF_EXT made the emitted extension depend on how devkit was RUNNING, so search-steering has two prior spellings (.mjs from a packaged install, .mts from a source-context one) and therefore two table rows sharing a single current command. Reconciliation picked its match with .find(), so a ledger row already carrying the CURRENT command — the crash-window state, where publishPlan wrote the ledger and died before the document — matched the FIRST projection by its current-command arm and authorised stripping only the .mjs spelling. A consumer whose document still held .mts got the dead hook stranded and the current command installed beside it: precisely the duplicate-orphan failure the crash-window arm exists to prevent, reintroduced through the arm itself. The unit test missed it because it exercised the crash window with the .mjs spelling only, which is the one .find() happens to return. Ruling refined: a claimed row authorises stripping EVERY prior spelling of that registration at the location the row names, not just the spelling the row itself holds. Sound on ownership grounds because devkit is the sole writer of those strings and the location gate is unchanged, and necessary because a row carrying the current command carries no information about which prior spelling the document still has. Regression covered by an it.each over both extensions, so a future single-spelling assumption fails on the .mts leg. Found by commit-guard and correctness-reviewer independently at the ship gate, both escalation-confirmed.

ruling: A confident PASS is cached at the altitude of the question the judge answers, not uniformly on the evidence bytes. Completeness judges the commit MESSAGE's claims against what the change delivers, so its PASS is additionally keyed on branch + normalised message + reviewer brief (version-salted), beside the byte-exact key. A retry that reshapes the diff to satisfy a DIFFERENT reviewer, on the same branch under the same message, is not re-judged. A FAIL is never sticky. Message normalisation mirrors git --cleanup=whitespace so the ship's composed temp file and git's COMMIT_EDITMSG compute one identical key across the two hooks.
note: sc-3468 — domain-reviewer PASSes now record the base they were judged against (base_sha on the review-cache entry, stamped from the gate's pinned base at settle), for NARRATION only: reuse across a rebase is unchanged (reviewers.mts cacheKey still keys on diff identity alone). A cache hit whose stored base differs from this run's base names both on its line, carries judged_base_sha + base_state on cache_hit and review_scope, and the provenance line claims the run's base only for reviewers that actually ran. REJECTED — keying the PASS on (diff, base): it re-opens the cost this Target settled on every rebase. Deferred: completeness and decision-alignment, which print no base and so make no false base claim.

ruling: devkit prove-regression is a generic evidence-capture command over two explicit commit refs and one exact argv vector. It executes that argv in independent unregistered disposable clones, requires red nonzero and green zero for a CAPTURED result, retains stdout/stderr plus hashes, records immutable SHAs plus cleanup and caller boundary-sample facts, and never calls exit polarity causal proof. An optional standard Vitest JSON report path adds reconciled structured counts and bounded red failure summaries; when requested, a missing or malformed report makes the result inconclusive. Test availability at both refs is the caller responsibility; direct relationship to the ticket and whole-suite sufficiency remain explicit human review claims. Commands are trusted and unsandboxed: inherited repository-local GIT_* overrides are stripped; POSIX process groups or marked descendants are supervised, while Windows safely terminates only the direct helper through its retained process handle. Boundary fingerprints are non-atomic samples, and deliberate ownership evasion or Windows descendants that outlive their parent are outside the portable guarantee. Temporary evidence roots must resolve outside the caller repository.
note: PR #530 review hardening: each operand now receives an independent copy-on-write-when-available dependency tree. Contained absolute links are rewritten into the completed snapshot, then all links are validated there and unsafe snapshots are removed, so red cannot mutate the caller store or contaminate green even if the source changes while it is copied. Directory links remain unprivileged junctions on Windows. Windows capture registers only SIGHUP, SIGINT, and SIGBREAK. This removes two accepted portability/mutability risks without changing the explicit-ref, exact-argv, non-causal CAPTURED contract.

ruling: Split by ownership. ruling: Both halves are devkit's. (1) devkit ship adopts runManagedPackagedScript, as devkit review already did: the script gets its OWN process group and signals are forwarded to that group, not to the wrapper alone. (2) Because SIGKILL is uncatchable, signal forwarding can never be sufficient, so every ephemeral ship worktree writes a run record — pid, start-time identity, gate supervisor pid, the base it was cut from, and whether this run created the branch — into the worktree's git ADMIN dir, where it outlives the worktree directory, is deleted for free by worktree remove/prune, and cannot reach a commit. A preflight reads that record before the branch is read and reclaims the worktree and branch ONLY when the record proves abandonment; otherwise it refuses naming the live pid, or reports and falls through. The governing invariant is no record, no destructive action: an unattributable worktree is never touched.
note: sc-2261 — the preflight now attributes the branch's holder to the CALLER'S OWN worktree (compared by git admin dir, never by filesystem path) and prints the two commands that free it. Previously a linked worktree was told to force-remove the tree it was executing inside, and a main tree got 'switch it off' without naming what to switch to. Same 'reports and falls through' clause, no new destructive path. Paired with a PR-base preflight: the DEFAULT base (this checkout's branch) is now proven to be a branch ON ORIGIN before the worktree, the commit and the push, so shipping from a provisioned worktree's local-only scratch branch refuses early instead of pushing a branch whose PR then cannot open; and the post-push PR-create hint re-verifies the recorded base on origin: it KEEPS that base when the branch is still there, and also when the re-verify itself fails (only ls-remote exit 2 proves absence), because gh fails for causes unrelated to the base and swapping a deliberately chosen one would retarget the PR; it names a different base only when the recorded one has genuinely left origin, and says so.

ruling: devkit ship gains an opt-in --wait-ci (with --wait-ci-timeout, default 900s) that polls the PR's checks after every artifact is durable. Its governing property is that the wait OBSERVES a PR that already exists rather than describing what shipped, and five behaviours follow from that. (1) It is not recorded in the ship-intent record and is not replayed by --resume, exactly as --ready is not; it is accepted under --resume so a retry can re-request it. (2) devkit ship exits 0 whenever the PR opened; the verdict rides one machine-readable stderr line plus a ship_ci telemetry row, never the exit code, because ship's exit status already means 'did the PR open' and an agent reading non-zero would retry --resume against a record the push already deleted. (3) ALL checks are polled; --required is never the default. (4) A terminal tally must hold for a wall-clock settle grace, not merely for N polls. (5) gh's non-zero exits are DATA: exit 8 is pending and still carries the rows on stdout, exit 1 with 'no checks reported' is an empty set.

note: sc-1711 — The sc-1550 receipt above was being DESTROYED for exactly the ships it exists to rescue. run-gates-with-capture.sh read tee's drain status with a bare 'wait tee_pid', and bash >= 4 returns 128+signum from that wait whenever a trapped signal is PENDING, without collecting the job. So a tee that had drained and exited 0 read as 143, the runner then blamed a gate log that had persisted perfectly ('could not persist gate output'), rc flipped 0 to 1, and ship-branch.sh correctly refused to mint refs/devkit/ship-receipts/<branch> for rc=1 — for a commit that had ALREADY LANDED with every gate green. The retry then hard-failed with 'no matching prior-ship gate receipt' and re-paid the whole chain: the precise cost this Target rules against, reintroduced by a status misread rather than by a policy. Falsified belief, load-bearing and the same class as the two EPERM/exit-4 notes above: 'a non-zero tee_status means the gate log could not be persisted'. It also means 'the operator pressed Ctrl-C'. Why it hid: bash 3.2 COLLECTS on the first read and returns tee's real status, and macOS ships 3.2 as /bin/bash, so the failure was 100 percent reproducible on Linux CI and unobservable on a stock mac — measured 5/5 red under bash 5.3.15 and 5/5 green under 3.2.57 against the verbatim runner. Fix: read the status a SECOND time, which returns tee's own. It must stay an if and never become a loop — a child that genuinely died of a signal reports 128+signum on EVERY re-read (measured 143/143/143 on both shells), so a loop would spin forever on the runner's own drain-escalation kill of tee. It also cannot be jobs-probe-guarded like the supervisor re-wait 45 lines above, because after an interrupted wait the job has already left the output of jobs -pr and jobs -ps. Guarded on drain_stage being 0 so the self-kill path is structurally excluded rather than comment-excluded. Rejected: discarding ANY status above 128 — measured to fail OPEN when tee exits 1 AND a signal arrives, since the first read is 143 either way and the real failure is recoverable only via the second read; that variant would have minted a receipt for a commit whose gate log really was truncated. Two residuals knowingly accepted: a signal delivered to the process GROUP kills tee for real (reads above 128 twice, fails closed — correct, the log truly was cut), and a second signal landing between the two reads degrades to the old behaviour. Scope is ship-only: GATE_SIGNAL_DEFER_EXIT is set at exactly one site (ship-branch.sh), so on review and reship forward_gate_signal exits inside the trap before the banner is reachable — which is why the review-side drain test stayed green throughout. Reship asymmetry left open deliberately: it never defers its signal exit, so it has no receipt to lose. STILL OPEN, different axis (gate-telemetry-self-describing): commit-with-gate-capture.sh emits ship_result from inside commit_with_gate_capture, which never sees REQUESTED_SIGNAL_STATUS — pre-fix every signalled ship wrote a phantom blocked_gate of 'unknown', post-fix it writes exit_code 0 for a ship that exits 143. Closer to true, still not 'interrupted'. Guard: the durable regression test resolves a bash >= 4 from PATH and SKIPS LOUDLY when it cannot find one, because the ship-branch integration test hardcodes /bin/bash and therefore cannot fail on a mac.

note: One supervised gate-capture path for ship/reship/review (sc-1199). Ship/reship previously took a second, weaker path — coreutils `timeout` plus a bare `  tee` — whose process-group kill fired ONLY on expiry. A reviewer that REJECTED exited in seconds, so the ceiling never fired, and any child the gate leaked kept the capture pipe's write-end open: `tee` never saw EOF, the run never returned, its EXIT trap never ran, and the ephemeral worktree stayed checked out, blocking the re-ship of the corrected snapshot. The supervisor now also reaps on this path: once the leader exits with a group still alive, a 5s linger grace precedes the same group-kill escalation, and the leader's status SURVIVES the reap so a rejection is never reported as a timeout (a converge-and-retry hint for a verdict that cannot converge on its own). Chosen over (a) a bounded tee-drain on the weak path — unwedges the shell but leaves the leaked judge tree alive burning subscription quota, and (b) spawning judges detached — puts them in their own group, which is precisely what the supervisor's escape-adoption exists to chase, and fixes only one leak source. Consequences: hang protection no longer depends on coreutils being installed (node + /bin/ps only), which retires that dependency for consumers and un-gates three hung-gate tests that never ran on stock macOS; the telemetry archive is now probed before it reaches tee so an unwritable path still cannot fail a ship; expiry is exactly 124 and 137 now unambiguously means the supervisor itself was SIGKILLed. ruling: In append mode every briefed path is compared, before any copy, against an ANCHOR: the blob this checkout last shipped for that path on this branch, read from the reconcile manifest (an op:delete record anchors on absence). A path with no record anchors at merge-base(PR tip, caller HEAD); unrelated histories anchor on the tip itself, which is the old copy. Tip unmoved since the anchor, or tip already equal to the caller's copy: copy, byte-identical to before. Caller unchanged since the anchor: keep the tip. Both changed a regular file: git merge-file, staged when clean. A conflict, a binary, symlink or gitlink both changed, or a delete/modify pair refuses before gates, naming up to three commits on the tip since the anchor; GUARD_SHIP_REPLACE_OK=1 copies the caller's file instead, as for new ships. The manifest keeps recording the CALLER's blob for a merged path, never the merged one: recording the merge would make the next re-push see an unmoved tip and copy the still-stale file, the same revert one ship later. Rewrite mode (--pr --base) is unchanged.
note: A manifest record whose blob is no longer in the object store anchors like no record (merge-base fallback): a merged path records the caller's blob, which no commit holds, so git gc can prune it while the PR is still open. Index writes normalise the briefed path, so a ./-spelled path stages as it did under git add.

label: L
ruling: Explicit paths remain the default for dirty-tree shipping. The opt-in --from-branch mode requires an explicit remote base, pins the base and current HEAD commits, proves ancestry, derives root-literal committed path membership, refuses in-scope overlays and unsupported path representations, and records branch source mode plus frozen membership for resume.
note: The explicit-path directory refusal names every directory argument in one message and its remedy prints the CHANGED set under them (git diff --name-only --no-renames HEAD plus git ls-files -o --exclude-standard, framed on the repo root) instead of git ls-files, which listed every tracked file and over-briefed (sc-2514). The check lives in one helper sourced by ship-branch.sh and reship.sh, and a symlink pointing at a directory now passes because git treats it as a file. Ship prints the command rather than expanding the directory, so the per-file isolation of explicit mode is unchanged. A --staged / --paths-from brief was requested and DECLINED under Rejected (a): the shared index is no more owned than the dirty tree in a shared checkout, and --from-branch remains the derived mode. Scope: cli/lib/ship/refuse-dir-paths.sh,cli/lib/ship/ship-branch.sh,cli/lib/ship/reship.sh,skills/using-devkit/SKILL.md

label: L
ruling: Every synced gate, script and asset resolves directory roots from the consumers guard.config.json (scanRoots, structure.trees, review roots), never a hardcoded stack layout. Docs frame any concrete layout as a labelled example, not universal. Conservative fallback (all-staged, or the electron DEFAULT_ROOTS) when config is absent — never match-nothing.
note: feature-critique shipped as a synced agent that reads guard.config.json + decision-log presence at RUNTIME (config-at-runtime, decisions-conditional) instead of baking a layout — conforms like the reviewer agents; rejected a sync-time generator that would re-bake the coupling.

label: W
ruling: devkit own test processes inherit NO run authority from whatever launched them. vitest.setup.mjs deletes an explicit, named list of ship/review authority variables before any test module loads (setupFiles runs per worker ahead of the first import, so even a top-level process.env capture sees the cleaned env), and both vitest configs share that one file. The list is the same vocabulary cli/lib/ship/review-target.sh unsets, bound to it by a parity test so the two can never drift; membership is reused, the reason is not (that script prevents inheriting a FOREIGN run authority). Deliberate invocation knobs are never scrubbed: SHIP_COMMIT_TIMEOUT and DEVKIT_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT are inputs a caller chose. A test that needs a policy var sets it explicitly. The guarantee is about INHERITANCE, not visibility - a per-worker setup file cannot undo a test that sets a var mid-file and never restores it.
note: sc-2259 follow-up — the Target's ruling said the scrub list IS review-target.sh's vocabulary; edge-case testing showed that list is not a superset of what a ship actually exports, so the first implementation was a partial fix. ship-branch.sh additionally exports DEVKIT_SHIP_BRANCH, DEVKIT_SHIP_DRY_GATES, DEVKIT_SHIP_FROM_BRANCH, DEVKIT_SHIP_INTENT_RECORDED, DEVKIT_SHIP_PATHS, DEVKIT_SHIP_REPO, DEVKIT_SHIP_RESUMED and DEVKIT_SHIP_ROOT, none of which review-target.sh unsets because it guards a review ENTRYPOINT rather than the downstream tree. Four of those are read at runtime and are not inert: qavis-advisory shipMode() branches on DEVKIT_SHIP_ROOT and then runs git -C against that path, and review completeness verdictBranch() scopes a sticky verdict to DEVKIT_SHIP_BRANCH, so an inherited pair makes a test answer for the OUTER ship's repository. The scrub now carries three provenance lists - INHERITED_RUN_ENV (review-target.sh parity), SHIP_EXPORTED_ENV (the ship-script delta) and TEST_ONLY_ADDITIONS (the FRINK_AI_STRICT alias) - with SCRUBBED_ENV as their union. The binding test no longer trusts a hand-written list: it parses the export left-hand sides out of ship-branch.sh and run-gates-with-capture.sh and requires every DEVKIT_/GUARD_ name found there to be scrubbed, so a future ship export is caught at the source rather than after it flips a gate test. Also pinned: vitest.e2e.config.mjs shares the same setupFiles, which was assumed rather than asserted.

label: L
ruling: Vendor third-party agent assets into devkit's own skills/ tree, pinned by FULL upstream commit SHA plus a sha256 of the vendored bytes (cli/lib/install/vendored-skills.mts, asserted by vendored-skills.test.mts). Delegating to the upstream installer ('claude plugin marketplace add' + 'claude plugin install') is REJECTED: Claude-only, writes to the user's GLOBAL config rather than the repo, needs the network at install time, and cannot be drift-checked or deselected. A SHA rather than a version range because these upstreams publish no tags — the SHA is the only stable identifier for the bytes that were reviewed. The upstream LICENSE ships BESIDE the asset rather than being folded into its frontmatter: that satisfies MIT attribution while keeping the asset byte-identical to upstream, so the recorded hash stays an exact upstream comparison. Pin refreshes are a deliberate maintainer act via scripts/sync-vendored-skills.mjs (network; never called by init/upgrade).
note: i-have-adhd now also registers a UserPromptSubmit anchor (agents-hooks/adhd-prompt-anchor.mjs), not just the SessionStart body. Evidence: the body enters context once and then sits at a fixed early position while the conversation grows — measured on this machine's own transcripts at up to 30 user turns and a peak of 1,002,118 context tokens between re-assertions. Instruction adherence falls over exactly that distance (MMMT-IF, arXiv 2409.18216: code-verified compliance 0.81 at turn 1 to 0.64 at turn 20 across Gemini 1.5 Pro / GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 Sonnet), and the intervention with direct causal evidence is proximity to the point of generation, not a higher-privilege channel: re-stating the constraints at the END of context recovered +22.3 points there, while the instructions had never left their original privileged position. Compaction is NOT the gap — SessionStart re-fires with source=compact and self-heals (verified against a real auto-compaction: preTokens 1002118, postTokens 20195). The gap is the long stretch between compactions. The anchor is deliberately ONE line restating only the rules that decay first, never the ~6.4KB body: redundant reinforcement is not free, and repetition reinforcing one instruction has been measured degrading adherence to others by up to 21.2% (arXiv 2602.04294), alongside the general irrelevant-context distractibility results (2302.00093, 2502.04362). Its closing clause preserves the skill's own explain-fully carve-out, without which a terse anchor pulls explanatory answers short. REJECTED: a fixed periodic cadence (every N turns) — no controlled sweep of reminder intervals exists in the literature, so any specific N would be invented; an output style is the only true system-prompt placement Claude Code offers but costs the single global outputStyle slot, defaults keep-coding-instructions to false (silently REPLACING the built-in coding instructions), is Claude-only, and per the same evidence would not fix drift anyway since it stays pinned at position 0. Note for future readers: hook additionalContext is normally delivered as a user-role system-reminder message, but 2.1.220 gates a genuine mid-conversation role:system path (beta mid-conversation-system-2026-04-07) whose exclusion list stops at claude-opus-4-7 — 4.8 and the 5-series fall through to a remote flag, so on those models this anchor may already arrive with true system authority. Cost is ~48 tokens per turn plus one node spawn; the spawn objection that kept the upstream ponytail tracker out is weaker here because consumer repos already spawn a UserPromptSubmit hook per prompt.

label: L
ruling: devkit BUNDLES the gate tools and runs them from its OWN install: jscpd via optionalDependencies (clone-detector resolves it hoist-agnostically from devkit's dir), and eslint + eslint-plugin-project-structure promoted to dependencies, driven by a new guard-structure bin that lints via buildStructureConfigs. init stops adding jscpd/eslint/plugin/parser to consumers (electron keeps its consumer-side preset).
note: structure:true now emits the single Devkit-owned guard-structure staged runner. It reads configured roots, validates normal staged files once, probes structural renames/deletions from an existing sibling where possible, and defers mixed index/worktree input to CI rather than declaring it checked. Electron still uses its pinned local ESLint preset behind that runner; config-driven stacks continue through Devkit’s bundled ESLint.
